summary: Regression certification for the PyMuPDF -> pypdfium2 (PDFium) swap in ocr_service.ocr_pdf. Reused /app/backend/tests/ (no test edits needed). Pytest: 25/27 PASS. Frontend Playwright: all 4 required UX paths PASS — scanned.pdf via PDFium rasterizer renders OCR tesseract:deu+eng badge with German content; german_doc.jpg image OCR renders ocr-badge; S3 sync renders without ocr-badge (correct); async + s.docx -> 202 PENDING -> COMPLETED. The CHANGED scanned-PDF path is GREEN end-to-end. However, ONE NEW HIGH-PRIORITY REGRESSION introduced by the swap: blank/empty PDF now returns HTTP 500 (was 422) because pypdfium2 raises PdfiumError on load ('Failed to load document (PDFium: Success).') which is wrapped as OCRError and falls through to the generic 500 handler instead of being mapped to ConversionError -> 422. The async path for blank.pdf also surfaces the raw PDFium error string instead of the expected 'no extractable text' message. All other 9 formats, OCR image, Ausweis detection, German char round-trip, multipart upload, S3, async OCR, auth/RBAC, X-Correlation-Id all behave correctly.

critical.issue: Returns 500 instead of 422 problem+json. After the PyMuPDF -> pypdfium2 swap, a zero-page/blank PDF causes pdfium.PdfDocument(path) to raise PdfiumError('Failed to load document (PDFium: Success).'). ocr_service.ocr_pdf wraps it as OCRError. extraction_pipeline._convert_path / _to_markdown does NOT catch OCRError -> mapped to generic 500 by FastAPI default handler instead of ConversionError -> 422 'no extractable text'.

Job status FAILED but error field is the raw pypdfium2 message 'OCR failed for PDF: Failed to load document (PDFium: Success).' instead of the expected user-friendly 'no extractable text' message. Same root cause as the sync 500.

action_items: Catch pypdfium2 load failure on empty/zero-page PDFs in services/extraction_pipeline.py::_convert_path (the .pdf branch) OR in services/ocr_service.py::ocr_pdf: when pdf load fails or len(pdf)==0, return '' instead of raising OCRError, so _to_markdown raises ConversionError('no extractable text...') -> 422.
Alternative: add OCRError -> ConversionError translation in extraction_pipeline (treat any OCRError that results in no text as 'no extractable text').
After fix, both test_sync_blank_pdf_returns_422_problem_json and test_async_blank_pdf_polls_to_failed must turn green.
Optional hardening: also try pdf load with try/except and explicitly check len(pdf)==0 to emit a deterministic 'no extractable text' message for both sync (422) and async (FAILED error field).
critical_code_review_comments: ocr_service.ocr_pdf wraps EVERY pypdfium2 exception (including load failures) into OCRError, but OCRError is NOT a registered FastAPI exception handler — it bubbles to the generic 500. Either translate OCRError to ConversionError in extraction_pipeline._convert_path, or register an OCRError handler that maps to 422 when the failure mode is 'document has no readable content'.

ocr_max_pages guard is properly applied via min(total, settings.ocr_max_pages) and a warning log — good. But there is no fallback if len(pdf) returns 0 (valid but empty PDF) — that path currently returns '' which would be correctly mapped to 422 via _to_markdown's empty check; the regression is strictly the PdfDocument(path) constructor failure path on malformed/empty xref PDFs.
Recommend exposing settings.ocr_max_pages via /api/health metadata for ops visibility.
Carryovers from iter4 still valid (build_provider silent mock fallback; 4xx retried in _attempt; CORS allow_credentials with '*'; mock _note field debug-gating).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Single remaining blocker: blank.pdf 500 regression caused by pypdfium2.PdfDocument(path) raising PdfiumError on malformed/empty PDFs. Fix is small (catch in extraction_pipeline.py or ocr_service.py) and the existing 2 failing tests (test_sync_blank_pdf_returns_422_problem_json + test_async_blank_pdf_polls_to_failed) will validate. Everything else (the actual CHANGED scanned-PDF rasterizer path, German OCR, Personalausweis detection, all 9 formats, RBAC, RFC 7807, X-Correlation-Id, async polling, frontend UX) is GREEN.
rca of the issue: PyMuPDF (fitz) silently opened blank.pdf and returned 0 text, which _to_markdown then translated to ConversionError('no extractable text...') -> 422. pypdfium2.PdfDocument(path) is stricter and raises PdfiumError('Failed to load document (PDFium: Success).') for the same fixture (a 912-byte ReportLab PDF with no pages). ocr_service.ocr_pdf wraps it in OCRError; there is no exception_handler for OCRError in main.py, so FastAPI's default 500 handler responds. Repro: curl -X POST $BASE/api/v1/extract/sync -H 'Authorization: Bearer $JWT' -F 'file=@/tmp/blank.pdf;type=application/pdf' -F 'instructions=x' -> 500 problem+json. Mitigation (any one): (a) ocr_service.ocr_pdf catches load failures and returns '' so empty-markdown path triggers; (b) extraction_pipeline._convert_path wraps the ocr_pdf call in try/except OCRError -> raise ConversionError('no extractable text...'); (c) register OCRError -> 422 handler in main.py.
